chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: :wave:

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: hey Bas, thanks for joining

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: Verification is very fast. Signing is slower than ECC, but faster than RSA.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: how much slower is FN-DSA when not using floating-point arithmetic, for signing / validation?

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: It used to be 20x, but the new approach is only approx 2x slower or less. Depends on platform of course, etc etc.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: both signing/validation?

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: Floating point only affects signing. Verification is very fast and doesn't use floating point.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: great. thank you.

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Seems FN-DSA will spillover the UDP truncation limit for DNSKEY queries and NXDOMAIN.

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: Shumon: even two FN-DSA signatures in response goes to 1300+ bytes

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Yup.

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: Would MTL need its own security analysis?

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: My informal list of ML-DSA implementations and test sites: https://github.com/paulehoffman/ml-dsa-in-dnssec

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: if we knew now which alg we like, how long would it take to get the root signed with that?

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: we are about to roll out a KSK that was generated in 2024. That's without an algorithm change.

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: I have more confidence in FN-DSA by 2029, but I have been very wrong about NIST before.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: we have never done a root zone KSK algorithm chane

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: so I have some doubts that we could achieve an algorithm roll by 2031

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: @joe: so min 2 year, my guess'd be probable 4+ years?

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: IANA has announced that the next root signing key will be ECDSA.

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: the one introduced next week?

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: Nonono. The one after that.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: no, there's a 2-year plan published this year

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Next week's is still RSA.

chat.author: Swapneel Sheth
chat.text: For MTL, We have done security analysis and published the research - https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1730. We welcome additional analysis.  Its  build on FIPS standards.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: I think an algorithm roll to ecdsa will be great, and I had not heard of that plan, thanks Paul. But a roll to an algorithm with a substantially greater response size impact, plus presumably more limited support in validators that might require dual-signing...

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: MTL should also radically reduce validator CPU burden

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: I'm sure the patent issue with MTL could probably be handled but I am less confident about the protocol changes

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: is there any argument that MTL could help increase the proportion of signed zones generally?

chat.author: Christian Elmerot
chat.text: What about MTL and live signing also

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: I'm wondering how high churn dynamic updated zones work with MTL however... do I need to change how I build zones to do periodic build + sign instead of dynamically updating the zone on an ongoing/continuous basis...?

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: (I asked last question 'cuase if we're gonna change DNSSEC a lot, that change should aim for more signed zones)

chat.author: Swapneel Sheth
chat.text: Protocol changes are not needed for the the base MTL

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: my sense is that we need to address the transport limitations that threaten large responses anyway, for a variety of reasons. And if we do that we have the luxury of caring a lot less about response sizes in dnssec

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: DNSSEC deployment is.... lagging (to be nice;-) if we're gonna change it, we should address that elephant

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: @Joe Abley: True

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: I think we can totally replace dnssec with something that is more deployable, and meet a 3031 deadline no problem

chat.author: Kazunori Fujiwara
chat.text: I would like to know if it is possible to operate frequently changing zones—such as .com or .net—in MTL mode.

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: I am particularly interested in whether MTL creates a logical path to "DNSSEC transparency".  The WebPKI has demonstrated the utility of a hash-tree transparency log system, and I would like to see the same for DNSSEC.

chat.author: Stefan Ubbink
chat.text: as far as I understood it is possible to do frequent delta updates with MTL

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: If there is a mass migration to secure DNS transports before PQC doomsday, how much do we care about DNS response sizes caused by larger signatures/keys?

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text:
"Verisign grants to any party a non-sublicenseable, world-wide, non-exclusive, no-charge, irrevocable (except as provided below) license to each Essential Claim to make, use, sell, offer for sale and import products and/or services that implement the Specification solely for use with DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC); provided, Verisign retains the sole and exclusive right to:
(i) terminate the above license"
[...]

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Ben - yes, I care about the DNSSEC Key Transparency solution too.

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: There have been some efforts in that area in the past, but they didn't go anywhere.

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: (the IPR is the common mutual self destruction clause)

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: I was distracted by the chat, did paul say he was doing one query/response transaction per TCP session, or is he exchanging multiple messages over the same session?

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: @Shumon I can imagine a cross-sign from a log operator, with the meaning "I have logged this entire subtree".

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: Is this one query per fresh TCP connection?

chat.author: Allison Mankin
chat.text: Mukund +1, I missed this too

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: I think session reuse is critical to understanding the performance impact of TCP

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: Did you enable server-side passive TCP fastopen (it's off by default on Linux distros).

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: i didnt know you could still buy RAM for $500

chat.author: Vladimír Čunát
chat.text: Clients doing TCP fast open seem rather rare in practice anyway.

chat.author: Sara Dickinson
chat.text: And how many simultaneous clients did he use?

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: What about RPS, etc. ?

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: hopefully there is a writeup in addition to these slides

chat.author: Stefan Ubbink
chat.text:
Sara Dickinson said:

And how many simultaneous clients did he use?

1 client system with xdpgun

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: unless under attack and people send spoofed TCP RST packets? then it gets much worse

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text:
Benjamin Schwartz said:

I am particularly interested in whether MTL creates a logical path to "DNSSEC transparency".  The WebPKI has demonstrated the utility of a hash-tree transparency log system, and I would like to see the same for DNSSEC.

The key problem here is rate-limiting.

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: The key problem for DNSSEC is almost no zones are secured with DNSSEC

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: yes, "don't use DNSSEC" is actually the current chosen solution :-)

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: sadly, yep

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: the key key problem is people are putting more data needing authentication into unsigned dns :)

chat.author: Vladimír Čunát
chat.text: DNSSEC usage is good in a couple countries/ccTLDs, but not globally, sadly.

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Yes, there are pockets of high usage, but across the entire Internet, deployment is embarassingly low.

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: are those "good" countries all ones where the TLD offers incentives to registrars for DNSSEC?

chat.author: Allison Mankin
chat.text: Speaking to several of these: in our (PCH) experience , many ccTLD authoritatives  in small countries experience serious performance issues when forced to TCP.   It is something of a limited mindset to test with new up-to-date hardware and assume that globally diverse authoritatives can update physical systems and fix TCP problems in a couple year timeframe.  And, as Vladimir just wrote, the ccTLDs have a high adoption of DNSSEC at the TLD.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: I hear you Wes!

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: If TCP can cost up to 25x in performance, does that screw our DoT aspirations?

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: I was hoping for some radical new ideas in the Chinese competition, but there weren't big surprises.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: Paul, sure not an overview of 70 algs :) I meant such that we get to know the promising ones.

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: (I didn't ask how they get broken so quickly)

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: As a data point, we had one of our PoP getting almost 100% of the queries to the authoritative servers there over TCP recently. That was surprising and exciting, and hopefully I can talk about it someday. But we noticed because one of our coders spotted it on some Grafana graph, so nothing broke!

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: test

chat.author: Bas Westerbaan
chat.text: More people measuring is better of course! Test zones under dnstest.dev

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: I would have assumed that some positive recommendation from dnsop would be needed before the root zone would be signed with a new alg

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: maybe not formally but...

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text:
+1 to Ben's observation.
TCP edges do not have to be overbuilt by the same factor!

chat.author: Mukund Sivaraman
chat.text: Latency is noticeable with UDP-TC-TCP

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: Stephen, this table indeed would likely first need to be updated: https://www.iana.org/assignments/dns-sec-alg-numbers#table-dns-sec-alg-numbers-1

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Yeah, but less with direct TCP.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: But not 0, for sure.

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: requring everyone to grow to a scale that supports TCP costs money, it's not just DoS.  We're out of time, but at one point B-Root did have issues scaling with TCP loads we were getting.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Skill issue, Wes. ;) (Totally kidding!) <3)

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: :p

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: I was speaking more to Ben

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: doesnt this all depend on the future of the dnsop wg and what to do, which we provided into to Med / Wes to for 2 years ?

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: I can't speak to that, so look at Med.  No idea what the IESG decided.

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: @Wes: I would call it an "engineering maturity" investment, rather than literal "scale".  But yes, it requires some work to tune timeouts, defenses, etc.

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: But my data collection for that survey was about 4 months, not 2 years :-P

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: @Ben Yes, you could just say "we just centralize everything to big players and let them sink the cost".

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: All small CCTLDs should start outsourcing?

chat.author: Mohamed Boucadair
chat.text: @Paul: expect an update on that SOON

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: In a TCP-heavy world, I can imagine that the open-source server defaults get tuned to handle it quite efficiently.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: I expect the same consistency and predictability from TCP session handling as we have from authoritative server selection. ;-)

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: HTTP services have spent years tuning both their software AND the OSes they run on.

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: I want all those ccTLDs to run DoT!

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: it requires kernel tuning too (see paul's presentation)
